summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and cardiomyopathy was admitted for shortness of breath and low-grade fevers. A chest X-ray showed right lower lobe opacity concerning for pneumonia, though her symptoms and lab findings were atypical. She was initially treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics but was narrowed to levofloxacin. Due to her stable condition and personal obligations, she chose to leave against medical advice after a brief hospitalization. She was discharged on oral levofloxacin with recommendations for outpatient follow-up, including imaging and cardiac evaluation to further assess the cause of her dyspnea.
